What do you learn in medical school?

Follow albumin from biochemistry to clinical training and compare the medical curricula at Zielona Góra, Oxford, Harvard, Monash and Maastricht.

Inside the Zielona Góra medical curriculum

What happens to your knowledge of albumin after the matura? In the University of Zielona Góra (UZ) medical curriculum for the 2026/27 intake, you go from protein structure to measuring albumin in serum in your very first semester.

Semester 1 · biochemistry with chemistry

On the matura you explain how albumin carries fatty acids. At UZ you learn where it is made, how it contributes to oncotic pressure and why its concentration can fall. In the lab you measure albumin in serum. The whole course carries 9 ECTS and 120 contact hours: 30 of lectures, 60 of laboratory work and 30 of seminars. Passing the lab and seminar is required to sit the exam.

Biochemistry syllabus · Matura question 1.2
Semesters 2–12 · from patient care to kidney disease

Semester 2 includes a four-week patient-care placement. Semesters 3–4 cover physiology with clinical physiology. Internal medicine begins in semester 5 and nephrology appears in semester 7. Here you can revisit albumin and explain how losing it through the kidneys contributes to oedema. Semesters 11 and 12 include 130 and 140 clinical hours respectively in internal medicine alone.

SylabUZ · 2026/27 study plan

How do other medical schools organise this learning?

We chose a programme from each of the three highest-performing countries in the healthcare comparison below: Australia, the Netherlands and the UK. Harvard adds the US route after college. The ranking concerns patient care. The comparison here concerns course content and sequence.

Monash · Australia

On the five-year school-leaver route, years 1–2 cover anatomy, physiology, biochemistry and pharmacology, using patient cases among other methods. Students practise communication and have early hospital placements. Years 3–5 are mainly in hospitals and practices. One case can therefore bring together material listed under several subject names at UZ.

Monash · course outline
Maastricht · Netherlands

At bachelor level, students practise doctors’ tasks with peers and simulated patients. In the three-year master’s degree, five compulsory clinical rotations account for 66 weeks. A simulated consultation and a hospital placement offer different kinds of patient experience. From the 2026/27 intake, the bachelor’s is taught in Dutch.

Bachelor’s curriculum · Master’s curriculum
Oxford · United Kingdom

On the standard A100 course, early blocks pair biochemistry with medical genetics and physiology with pharmacology. The Patient and Doctor course runs alongside them. Students also complete a research project during the first three years. The main clinical phase spans years 4–6, with medicine and surgery rotations in year 4.

Oxford · A100 course structure
Harvard Pathways · United States

After college, MD students study foundations and integrated human pathophysiology alongside the longitudinal Practice of Medicine course. The main clinical clerkships (Principal Clinical Experience) begin in MD year 2. When comparing that with UZ year 2, count the time since secondary school as well.
